newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares mixed, seen stabilising this week. [CORRECTED 15:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Polish shares mixed, seen stabilising this week. [CORRECTED 15:50 GMT]

text.p: Most Polish shares fell in lower turnover but gains by some heavyweights pushed the main market up slightly and analysts said the bourse could be entering a stabilisation period.
The main market has risen 5.1 percent over three sessions after having dropped 14.6 percent in profit-taking since October 9's 30-month high.
"We should have stabilisation or a slight fall, levelling out some of the big growth we just had," said Mateusz Andrzejewski, an analyst at Bank Pekao SA brokerage.
Analysts saw no near-term positive signals.
The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.3 percent to 13,535.4 points and turnover fell 3.3 percent to 111.9 million zlotys on both markets.
Analysts said the profit-taking had accelerated after the lower house of parliament sought to cut taxes for low earners last month, but that no more deep falls were expected.

"The market has fallen so much that negative impulses already seem priced in," said Jan Koch, of Polish Development Bank (PBR) brokerage, adding that investors were disappointed that overall 1996 earnings were uninspiring and inflation at least two percent above the early year target of 17 percent.
Analysts said top gainer Espebepe, up 4.3 percent after jumping 9.5 percent last session, was enjoying speculative growth after having plunged on a bankruptcy threat.
Analysts said the low turnover that accompanied Kredyt Bank's 4.7-percent fall made it impossible to tell if Lithuania's rejection of its branch application had an impact.
NFI units were flat at 144 zlotys in regular bourse trade and fell 3.8 percent to 140 zlotys in live trade.
Continuous trade turnover was at 1.7 million zlotys with biggest mover Stalexport down 1.7 percent (corrects from "up 2.3 percent").
